events.title: Diffie–Hellman cryptography paper
events.summary: Whitfield Diffie and Martin Hellman published New Directions in Cryptography in November 1976 — introducing public-key exchange and the foundations of modern cryptography.
events.about: The Diffie–Hellman key exchange let two parties agree on a shared secret over an insecure channel — enabling TLS, SSH, and VPN handshakes today. The paper also articulated the vision of public-key cryptography that RSA would fulfill a year later.

narrative.whyChosen: Diffie–Hellman introduced the public-key paradigm to academic cryptography.
narrative.whyImportant: Key exchange without pre-shared secrets became the basis of secure internet protocols.
narrative.problemSolved: Symmetric-only crypto required costly secure channels to distribute keys at scale.
